question: What is the main goal of workplace ergonomics in nursing?

options.A: Reducing the number of patients assigned to each nurse
options.B: Eliminating the need for taking breaks during a shift
options.C: Fitting the work environment and equipment to the worker
options.D: Speeding up the documentation process on computer terminals

explanation: Spot on! Ergonomics is all about shaping your tools and workspace to match your body, making your daily tasks safer and more comfortable. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why is proper ergonomic design particularly important for healthcare professionals?

options.A: It replaces the need for physical therapy after an injury
options.B: It completely stops all infectious disease transmission in wards
options.C: It guarantees faster recovery times for admitted patients
options.D: It prevents physical fatigue and long-term musculoskeletal injuries

explanation: You got it! Nursing is physically demanding work, and good ergonomics helps protect your body from burnout and chronic aches. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h1)

question: What happens to the lower back curve of the spine when you slouch forward for a long time?

options.A: It locks into a permanently curved position
options.B: It stops the flow of cerebrospinal fluid completely
options.C: It becomes stronger and more flexible
options.D: It flattens and over stretches supporting ligaments

explanation: Exactly. Slouching flattens your natural lower back curve, putting a lot of unnecessary strain on the supporting soft tissues. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h2)

question: How does keeping your muscles tense for too long due to poor posture affect your body?

options.A: It builds permanent muscle mass faster than regular exercise
options.B: It increases the oxygen supply to the overworked muscle fibers
options.C: It cools down the body temperature in surrounding joints
options.D: It reduces adequate blood flow, leading to fatigue and pain

explanation: Spot on! Constant muscle tension squeezes your blood vessels, starving your muscles of oxygen and leaving you feeling sore and tired. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which common issue involves the compression of the median nerve in the wrist?
explanation: Well done! Carpal tunnel happens when the median nerve gets squeezed as it passes through your wrist into your hand. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h3)

question: A nurse who constantly tilts their head downward to read electronic charts is most at risk for what condition?
explanation: Correct! Straining your neck downward for long periods puts extra wear and tear on your neck bones over time. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h3)

question: Where should the top of a computer monitor be positioned relative to your eyes?

options.A: Far below chest height on the desktop
options.B: At or slightly below eye level
options.C: Turned sideways to your direct line of sight
options.D: Significantly higher than the top of the head

explanation: That's right! Keeping the top of the screen near eye level saves your neck from uncomfortable tilting up or down. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h4)

question: A nurse notices her wrists resting hard against the sharp edge of the desk while typing patient notes. What is the best immediate adjustment?

options.A: Wear a thick leather weightlifting belt to improve core stability while charting
options.B: Stand up completely for all future documentation tasks during the shift
options.C: Tilt the computer monitor upward by forty-five degrees to change her line of sight
options.D: Reposition the keyboard and adjust her chair so wrists stay straight and unsupported by sharp edges

explanation: Spot on! Keeping your wrists free from sharp desk edges prevents annoying nerve compression and soft tissue pain. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h4)

question: When moving a heavy medication cart down a hospital hallway, what is the safest technique?

options.A: Pull the cart behind you for better steering
options.B: Hold the cart with only one hand at all times
options.C: Push the cart rather than pulling it
options.D: Run quickly to minimize the duration of the push

explanation: You got it! Pushing lets you use your body weight and strong leg muscles instead of straining your back and shoulders. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why is gripping small mobile tablets with just one hand for a long time risky for nurses?

options.A: It can cause repetitive strain injuries in the fingers and thumbs
options.B: It reduces the wireless signal strength of the device
options.C: It permanently ruins the electronic screen display calibration
options.D: It causes immediate bone fractures in the wrist bones

explanation: Correct! Small, repeated hand movements without a break can easily irritate your tendons and nerves. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h5)

question: What does the popular 20-20-20 rule for eye health involve?

options.A: Drinking 20 ounces of water every 20 minutes at the desk
options.B: Taking a 20-minute nap every 20 hours of shift work
options.C: Adjusting screen brightness 20 times per shift
options.D: Looking at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds every 20 minutes

explanation: Spot on! This simple trick gives your eye muscles a much-needed break from staring at screens all day. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h6)

question: Which symptom is most common in nurses who spend long hours staring at computer screens for charting?
explanation: You got it! When we stare at screens, we tend to blink less, which leaves our eyes feeling dry and tired. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h6)

question: How long should a typical ergonomic micro-break last during a busy clinical shift?
explanation: Correct! Even super short, frequent pauses are enough to shake off muscle tension without slowing down your patient care. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h7)

question: Why is it smart to do quick stretches during natural pauses, like waiting for a computer system to load?

options.A: It is the only legal time management allows for stretching
options.B: It integrates injury prevention seamlessly into the existing workflow
options.C: It prevents the computer hardware from crashing unexpectedly
options.D: It doubles the processing speed of electronic health records

explanation: Spot on! Using your downtime for a quick stretch ensures you actually take care of your body despite a crazy busy schedule. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h7)

question: Whose responsibility is it to provide safe ergonomic equipment and policies in a hospital?

options.A: Only the individual nurse working night shifts
options.B: The patients admitted to the specific medical ward
options.C: The healthcare institution and facility management
options.D: The federal ministry of finance exclusively

explanation: Well done! Hospitals and facility management have a duty of care to ensure their staff have safe equipment and workspaces. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h8)

question: Why is it important to speak up and report physical discomfort early on?

options.A: It guarantees an immediate promotion to head nurse
options.B: It allows management to reduce the staff member's salary
options.C: It prevents minor aches from turning into disabling injuries
options.D: It is required before a nurse can take a lunch break

explanation: Exactly! Catching little aches and pains early means you can fix them before they turn into major health problems. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h8)
